guides.text:
TaktTools  ·  Downtime Log & Pareto guide
Page 1
Downtime Log & Pareto
Step-by-step guide: log every stop and see which causes cost the most time
What it does
You record each stop with a reason. The Pareto sheet ranks the reasons by minutes lost, with each
reason's share and the running total, so you can see the few causes behind most of your downtime.
Filter by date range and machine.
Yellow cells: type here.
Grey cells: calculated. Don't type over them.
The sheets
Sheet
What it's for
How to use
A one-page summary.
Setup
Your machines (up to 30) and your downtime reasons with categories (up to 30).
Downtime Log
One row per stop. Up to 1,000 rows.
Pareto
Reasons ranked by minutes lost, with a Pareto chart of the top 12.
By Machine
Downtime minutes and stop counts per machine.
Before you start
1
Open the file in your spreadsheet app (see Works with in the listing). If Excel shows a yellow
Protected View bar because the file was downloaded, click Enable Editing.
2
Save a copy under your own name (for example, add your plant or year) and keep the original
download as a clean spare.
3
Read the How to use sheet. It's a one-page summary of this guide.
Step 1: Set up machines and reasons
1
Go to the Setup sheet.
2
Under Machine, list your machines, one per row.
3
Under Downtime reason and Category, edit the 12 starter reasons to match how your plant talks
about stops. Keep the list short, about 10 to 15 reasons. Categories (Breakdown, Material, and so on)
can be renamed too.

TaktTools  ·  Downtime Log & Pareto guide
Page 2
Setup: machines on the left, reasons and categories on the right.
Step 2: Log every stop
1
Go to the Downtime Log sheet and use one row per stop.
2
Enter Date, Shift and Machine (from the drop-down).
3
Enter Start and End as times, like 7:15 and 7:50. A stop that crosses midnight, like 23:40 to 0:25, is
handled automatically (45 minutes).
4
If you only know how long it lasted, leave Start and End blank and type the minutes in Minutes (if no
start/end). Typed minutes always win over start and end times.
5
Pick a Reason from the drop-down. Duration, Category and Check fill in by themselves. Check
should say OK; otherwise it tells you what's missing, such as a date, a reason, or minutes that aren't
a number of 0 or more.
6
Add Notes if useful, especially for "Other".
7
The rows marked EXAMPLE show the expected format. When you're ready, select just their yellow
cells and press Delete to clear them. Don't delete whole rows: that removes the formulas in the grey
columns too.
Downtime Log with the example rows, including a stop that crosses midnight.

TaktTools  ·  Downtime Log & Pareto guide
Page 3
If Category shows Not in Setup, the reason was typed instead of picked, or is spelled differently from the Setup list. Its
minutes still count in the total, under Unclassified on the Pareto sheet. Pick the reason from the drop-down so it's
counted under the right reason. A row counts as a stop when its duration is more than 0 minutes; rows without a date, or
with invalid minutes, are left out of the totals.
Step 3: Read the Pareto
1
Go to the Pareto sheet.
2
Optional: set From date, To date and Machine. Leave any of them blank to include everything. Both
dates are included in the range.
3
Total downtime is every valid logged minute in the range. Unclassified shows minutes whose
reason is blank or not on the Setup list. Fix those in the log so they're ranked.
4
Read the table from the top: Rank, Reason, Minutes, Stops, % of total and Cumulative %.
Reasons with no minutes in the range are left out.
5
The chart shows the top 12 reasons as bars, with the cumulative % as a line on the right-hand axis.
6
Start improvement work with the reasons at the top. Often the first two or three account for most of
the lost time.
Pareto: reasons ranked by minutes, with cumulative % and the Pareto chart.
Step 4: Compare machines
The By Machine sheet shows total downtime, number of stops, average minutes per stop and each
machine's share of all downtime, plus No machine / not in Setup and All logged downtime rows so
the totals always add up. It uses the date range set on the Pareto sheet; the machine filter doesn't apply
here.

TaktTools  ·  Downtime Log & Pareto guide
Page 4
By Machine: downtime minutes, stops and share per machine.
Tips

If Other climbs into your top reasons, read its notes and add the missing reason to Setup.

Durations are rounded to whole minutes.

Log stops the same day, while people remember the cause.
Questions
The log is full (1,000 rows). What now? Save the workbook as a new file for the next period, clear the
yellow cells in the log, and keep going.
Can I rename the sheets or move columns? Please don't. The formulas refer to them by position.
Need help?
Message us through Etsy (the Message seller button on our shop or your order). Tell us which file,
which sheet, and what you typed. We answer questions about using the templates as described in this
guide; we can't do custom changes or set-up work.
These templates were designed with help from AI tools and checked by the seller.

TaktTools  ·  Manufacturing templates bundle guide
Page 1
OEE Tracker
Step-by-step guide: track Overall Equipment Effectiveness by machine and shift
What it does
You log one row per machine per shift. The workbook calculates Availability, Performance, Quality and
OEE for every row, then summarizes each machine on the Dashboard for any date range you choose,
with a chart and a comparison to your target.
Yellow cells: type here.
Grey cells: calculated. Don't type over them.
The sheets
Sheet
What it's for
How to use
A one-page summary.
Setup
Your machines and each one's ideal cycle time. Up to 20 machines.
Production Log
One row per machine per shift. Up to 500 rows.
Dashboard
Totals and OEE by machine for a date range, plus a chart.
Before you start
1
Open the file in your spreadsheet app (see Works with in the listing). If Excel shows a yellow
Protected View bar because the file was downloaded, click Enable Editing.
2
Save a copy under your own name (for example, add your plant or year) and keep the original
download as a clean spare.
3
Read the How to use sheet. It's a one-page summary of this guide.
Step 1: Set up your machines
1
Go to the Setup sheet.
2
In Machine, type each machine's name once, one per row (up to 20). Use the names your team
already uses.
3
In Ideal cycle time (seconds per part), enter the fastest time the machine can sustainably make one
good part. For a line, use the time per finished unit at rated speed. Example: a machine rated at 300
parts per hour has an ideal cycle time of 3600 / 300 = 12 seconds.
4
Clear the three EXAMPLE machines when you no longer need them (yellow cells only).
Getting the ideal cycle time right matters most: if it's too slow, Performance can show over 100% and the Check column
will flag it.
Step 2: Log each shift

TaktTools  ·  Manufacturing templates bundle guide
Page 2
1
Go to the Production Log sheet.
2
Fill in one row per machine per shift. The yellow columns are: Date, Shift (any label, e.g. Day or 1st),
Machine (pick from the drop-down), Shift length (min), Planned stops (min), Unplanned
downtime (min), Total parts and Rejected parts. Shift length and total parts are required; blank
planned stops, downtime or rejects count as 0.
3
Planned stops are times the machine isn't expected to run, like breaks and scheduled meetings.
Unplanned downtime is every other minute it was stopped: breakdowns, changeovers, waiting for
material.
4
The grey columns fill in by themselves, including OEE (coloured green, amber or red) and Check.
5
Look at Check on each new row. It should say OK. If not, see the table below. Rows with an error are
left out of the Dashboard until you fix them.
6
The rows marked EXAMPLE show the expected format. When you're ready, select just their yellow
cells and press Delete to clear them. Don't delete whole rows: that removes the formulas in the grey
columns too.
Production Log with the example rows. Yellow columns are typed in; grey columns calculate.
What the Check column means
Message
What to do
Machine not in Setup
The machine name isn't on the Setup sheet, or is spelled differently.
Pick it from the drop-down, or add it to Setup.
Set an ideal cycle time in Setup
The machine has no ideal cycle time (or 0) on the Setup sheet.
Enter numbers: shift length and total parts
are required
A required cell is empty, or a cell contains text instead of a number.
Values must be 0 or more (shift length
above 0)
A negative number, or a shift length of 0.
Rejects > total parts
Rejected parts must be part of the total. Fix one of the two numbers.
Planned stops >= shift length
Planned stops leave no time to run. Check both numbers.
Downtime > planned time
Unplanned downtime is longer than shift length minus planned stops.
Check the three time columns.
Check: performance above 100%
A warning only; the row still counts. The machine made parts faster
than its ideal cycle time allows. Usually the cycle time in Setup is too
slow, or the count is wrong.
OK
Nothing obviously wrong.

TaktTools  ·  Manufacturing templates bundle guide
Page 3
Step 3: Read the Dashboard
1
Go to the Dashboard sheet.
2
Optional: enter a From date and/or To date. Leave them blank to include every row. Both dates are
included in the range.
3
Set your OEE target (85% is filled in). OEE cells turn green at or above target, amber from 60% up
to the target, and red below 60%. OEE vs target shows the gap.
4
Each row adds up times and part counts first, then calculates the percentages, so a long shift counts
more than a short one. All machines OEE is total ideal time for good parts divided by total planned
production time, which stays correct when machines have different cycle times.
Dashboard: totals and OEE by machine, the all-machines total, and the OEE chart.
How the numbers are calculated
Measure
Formula
Planned production time
Shift length - planned stops
Run time
Planned production time - unplanned downtime
Availability
Run time ÷ planned production time
Performance
(Ideal cycle time × total parts) ÷ run time

TaktTools  ·  Manufacturing templates bundle guide
Page 4
Measure
Formula
Quality
Good parts ÷ total parts (good parts = total - rejected)
OEE
Availability × Performance × Quality = (ideal cycle time × good parts) ÷
planned production time
85% OEE is a commonly cited "world-class" benchmark. Many plants start well below it; improving against your own
baseline matters more.
Questions
The log is full (500 rows). What now? Save the workbook as a new file for the next period (for
example, one per quarter), clear the yellow cells in the log, and keep going.
Can I add more than 20 machines? Not in this version. Message us if you need more.
Can I rename the sheets or move columns? Please don't. The formulas refer to them by position.
Need help?
Message us through Etsy (the Message seller button on our shop or your order). Tell us which file,
which sheet, and what you typed. We answer questions about using the templates as described in this
guide; we can't do custom changes or set-up work.
These templates were designed with help from AI tools and checked by the seller.

TaktTools  ·  Manufacturing templates bundle guide
Page 9
Preventive Maintenance Schedule
Step-by-step guide: plan recurring maintenance and see what's due
What it does
You list each recurring maintenance task and how often it's due. Each time a task is done, you add a line
to the Completion Log. The plan then shows each task's last completion, next due date, days left and a
colour-coded status.
Yellow cells: type here.
Grey cells: calculated. Don't type over them.
The sheets
Sheet
What it's for
How to use
A one-page summary.
PM Plan
One row per asset and task, with status. Up to 300 tasks.
Completion Log
One row each time a task is done. Up to 2,000 rows.
Before you start
1
Open the file in your spreadsheet app (see Works with in the listing). If Excel shows a yellow
Protected View bar because the file was downloaded, click Enable Editing.
2
Save a copy under your own name (for example, add your plant or year) and keep the original
download as a clean spare.
3
Read the How to use sheet. It's a one-page summary of this guide.
Step 1: Build your plan
1
Go to the PM Plan sheet.
2
Add one row per asset and task. Fill in Asset, Task, Frequency (days) and Assigned to. The
frequency is a fixed number of days: 1 = daily, 7 = weekly, 14 = every two weeks, 30 = about monthly,
90 = about quarterly, 365 = about yearly.
3
If you know when a task was last done before you started using this workbook, enter that date in Last
done before log. Otherwise leave it blank: the task shows as due today, every day, until you log it or
enter a date.
4
Keep each asset + task combination on one row only. A repeated combination shows Duplicate row;
a blank, zero or negative frequency shows Check frequency. Both are counted under Needs fixing
at the top right.

TaktTools  ·  Manufacturing templates bundle guide
Page 10
5
The rows marked EXAMPLE show the expected format. When you're ready, select just their yellow
cells and press Delete to clear them. Don't delete whole rows: that removes the formulas in the grey
columns too.
PM Plan with example tasks, statuses and the counts box (top right).
Step 2: Log completed work
1
Go to the Completion Log sheet.
2
Each time a task is done, add a row: Date done, Asset and Task (pick both from the drop-downs so
they match the plan exactly), Done by and any Notes.
3
Check Matches plan?. It should say OK. Enter the date done means the date is missing. No
matching asset + task in plan means the asset or task is spelled differently from the PM Plan, so
the plan won't update. Fix the spelling.
Completion Log: each completion updates the plan.
Step 3: Read the plan
1
Back on PM Plan, the grey columns update automatically: Last completed (the most recent of the
logged dates and the before-log date), Next due, Days until due and Status.
2
OVERDUE (red) means the due date has passed. Due soon (amber) means it's due within the
window. OK (green) means it's not due yet.
3
Change the Due soon window (days) at the top of the sheet. It starts at 7.
4
The counts box at the top right shows how many tasks are Overdue, Due soon, OK, and Needs fixing.
5
To get this week's work list, sort or filter by Status: Data > Filter in Excel.
Dates and statuses use today's date from your computer, so they change from day to day. The example rows are set
relative to today for the same reason.
Questions

TaktTools  ·  Manufacturing templates bundle guide
Page 11

The Completion Log is full. Save the workbook as a new file, enter each task's most recent date in
Last done before log, clear the yellow cells in the log, and keep going.

to the Completion Log. The plan then shows each task's last completion, next due date, days left and a
colour-coded status.
Yellow cells: type here.
Grey cells: calculated. Don't type over them.

Before you start
1
Open the file in your spreadsheet app (see Works with in the listing). If Excel shows a yellow
Protected View bar because the file was downloaded, click Enable Editing.
2
Save a copy under your own name (for example, add your plant or year) and keep the original
download as a clean spare.
3
Read the How to use sheet. It's a one-page summary of this guide.
Step 1: Build your plan
1
Go to the PM Plan sheet.
2
Add one row per asset and task. Fill in Asset, Task, Frequency (days) and Assigned to. The
frequency is a fixed number of days: 1 = daily, 7 = weekly, 14 = every two weeks, 30 = about monthly,
90 = about quarterly, 365 = about yearly.
3
If you know when a task was last done before you started using this workbook, enter that date in Last
done before log. Otherwise leave it blank: the task shows as due today, every day, until you log it or
enter a date.
4
Keep each asset + task combination on one row only. A repeated combination shows Duplicate row;
a blank, zero or negative frequency shows Check frequency. Both are counted under Needs fixing
at the top right.

5
The rows marked EXAMPLE show the expected format. When you're ready, select just their yellow
cells and press Delete to clear them. Don't delete whole rows: that removes the formulas in the grey
columns too.

Step 2: Log completed work
1
Go to the Completion Log sheet.
2
Each time a task is done, add a row: Date done, Asset and Task (pick both from the drop-downs so
they match the plan exactly), Done by and any Notes.
3
Check Matches plan?. It should say OK. Enter the date done means the date is missing. No
matching asset + task in plan means the asset or task is spelled differently from the PM Plan, so
the plan won't update. Fix the spelling.
Completion Log: each completion updates the plan.
Step 3: Read the plan
1
Back on PM Plan, the grey columns update automatically: Last completed (the most recent of the
logged dates and the before-log date), Next due, Days until due and Status.
2
OVERDUE (red) means the due date has passed. Due soon (amber) means it's due within the
window. OK (green) means it's not due yet.
3
Change the Due soon window (days) at the top of the sheet. It starts at 7.
4
The counts box at the top right shows how many tasks are Overdue, Due soon, OK, and Needs fixing.
5
To get this week's work list, sort or filter by Status: Data > Filter in Excel.
Dates and statuses use today's date from your computer, so they change from day to day. The example rows are set
relative to today for the same reason.

What if a task is done early? Log the actual date. The next due date counts from the last completion.
The Completion Log is full. Save the workbook as a new file, enter each task's most recent date in
Last done before log, clear the yellow cells in the log, and keep going.
Can I rename the sheets or move columns? Please don't. The formulas refer to them by position.
